items.t: “버튼만 누르면 안약이 쏙”…KAIST, 우주서도 쓰는 안약 패치 개발
items.d: 중력이 거의 없는 우주에서도 버튼만 누르면 안약을 눈에 넣을 수 있는 착용형 패치가 개발됐다. 우주인의 눈 건강 관리뿐 아니라 손떨림이 심한 환자나 고령자의 자가 투약에도 활용될 전망이다.KAIST는 정기훈 바이오및뇌공학과 교수 연구팀이 우세준 분당서울대병원 교수 연구팀과 공동으로 착용형 안약 패치를 개발했다고 21일 밝혔다. 패치에는 비타민 C와 베이킹소다가 물과 만나면 이산화탄소가 발생하는 원리를 적용했다. 눈 주변에 패치를 붙이고 버튼을 누르면 내부에서 발생한 기체의 압력이 안약을 눈으로 밀어내는 방식이다. 별도의 전기 장치나 펌프 없이 작동한다.일반적인 안약은 고개를 젖혀 눈에 액체를 떨어뜨리는 방식이지만, 우주에서는 중력이 거의 없어 이를 사용하기 어렵다. 반면 이번에 개발한 패치는 중력에 의존하지

items.t: 로켓보다 AI가 효자…스페이스X, 매출 161% 급증 '깜짝 실적'
items.fullText: 테크 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 로켓보다 AI가 효자…스페이스X, 매출 161% 급증 '깜짝 실적' 입력 2026.10.21 08:54 수정 2026.10.21 08:54 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 이영애 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. AI 사업 매출 76억달러로 전체 52% 스타링크 가입자 1360만명으로 확대 3분기 AI 설비투자에 164억달러 투입 스페이스X 제공 일론 머스크 테슬라 최고경영자(CEO)가 이끄는 미국 우주기업 스페이스X가 인공지능(AI) 사업을 앞세워 시장 전망치를 웃도는 깜짝 실적을 거뒀다. 로켓 발사와 위성통신을 주력으로 삼던 스페이스X가 AI 인프라 기업으로 빠르게 변신하고 있다는 평가가 나온다. 스페이스X는 20일(현지시간) 올해 3분기 매출이 145억8000만달러(약 20조원)로 전년 동기 대비 161% 증가했다고 발표했다. 시장 전망치인 127억2000만달러를 크게 웃도는 수치다. 순이익은 44억달러로 시장 예상치(15억7000만달러)의 약 2.8배에 달했다. 지난해 같은 기간 11억달러 순손실을 기록한 데서 흑자로 돌아섰다. 실적 성장을 이끈 것은 AI 사업이다. AI 데이터센터와 소프트웨어 등을 포함한 '슈퍼인텔리전스(SI)' 부문 매출은 76억달러로 1년 전보다 830% 급증했다. 전체 매출의 52%를 차지하며 기존 주력인 위성통신 사업을 넘어섰다. 스페이스X는 앤트로픽과 구글, 리플렉션AI 등에 데이터센터 연산 능력을 제공하고 있다. AI 코딩 도구 '커서' 인수와 자체 AI 서비스 '그록'의 이용 확대도 실적에 기여했다. AI 모델 개발뿐 아니라 다른 기업에 컴퓨팅 인프라를 공급하는 사업이 새로운 성장 동력으로 떠오른 셈이다. 기존 위성통신 사업도 성장세를 이어갔다. 스타링크 등을 포함한 통신 부문 매출은 52억5000만달러로 전년 동기 대비 69% 증가했다. 스타링크 개인 가입자는 1360만명으로 늘었다. 통신 부문 영업이익은 약 23억7000만달러를 기록했다. 반면 로켓 발사 등을 포함한 우주 부문 매출은 약 18억달러로 전체의 12% 수준에 그쳤다. 스페이스X는 AI 인프라 투자에도 속도를 내고 있다. 3분기 설비투자 규모는 196억달러로, 이 가운데 164억달러가 AI 인프라에 투입됐다. 머스크 CEO는 실적 발표 콘퍼런스콜에서 "우리는 초지능 컴퓨팅 자원의 부족에 직면할 것이며, 이런 부족 현상은 오랫동안 지속될 것"이라고 말했다. 이영애 기자 0ae@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 이영애 ADVERTISEMENT 관련 뉴스 1 日도 '스페이스X식' 우주개발…H3 제작·발사 민간 일원화 일본이 주력 로켓 H3의 제작과 발사를 미쓰비시중공업으로 일원화한다. 정부 우주기관이 맡아 온 발사 업무를 민간에 넘겨 비용 경쟁력을 높이고 해외 위성 발사 수요를 확보한다는 구상이다. 민간기업이 제작부터 발사&mi... 2026.10.21 07:48 2 AI가 AI를 해킹하는 시대, 우리의 할일은? items.t: Musk Teases SpaceX-Tesla Merger in Earnings Call
items.d: Elon Musk said SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to explore a potential merger, a preliminary step toward what would rank as the largest corporate tie-up of all time. Ed Ludlow shares the details. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger
items.d: Elon Musk likes the idea but says he is not on either committee, which is made up of independent directors.
items.fullText: The boards of SpaceX and Tesla have each formed special committees to review a possible merger. The special committees, which consist of independent directors, were created at the request of shareholders, according to Elon Musk, CEO and the largest individual shareholder of both companies. “Because I’m a conflicted party, I can’t actually be in the discussions of the special committees, so it’s this sort of a … It’s an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking, and I can’t be in the conversation,” Musk said in response to a question during SpaceX’s third-quarter earnings call. Musk didn’t name the members of these special committees, only noting that they were independent directors. Tesla has seven independent board members under Nasdaq’s listing standards, including board chair Robyn Denholm; Ira Ehrenpreis, who is also a committee chair; former Tesla CTO JB Straubel; Joe Gebbia; Jack Hartung; James Murdoch; and Kathleen Wilson-Thompson, according to the company’s October 19 proxy filing . Neither Musk, nor his brother Kimbal Musk, are independent. Denholm, Gebbia, Ehrenpreis, Hartung, Murdoch, and Wilson-Thompson sit on a variety of established committees overseeing audit, compensation, and corporate governance. SpaceX lists six independent directors , including Ehrenpreis, who is also the chair of the company’s compensation and nominating committee. Randy Glein, Donald Harrison, Steve Jurvetson, Luke Nosek, and Roelof Botha are also considered independent directors. Antonio Gracias, Musk, and SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell are also on the board, but not considered independent. Gracias, who once sat on Tesla’s board, founded and leads Valor Equity Partners, which has a 3.4% stake in SpaceX. items.t: Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss merger idea
items.d: Musk said he isn’t a member of either special committee or involved in the talks because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations.
items.fullText: Business News Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees to discuss merger idea Musk said he isn’t a member of either special committee or involved in the talks because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk said he favored combining his two biggest companies. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 20, 2026, 6:57 PM EDT By David Ingram Tech billionaire Elon Musk said Tuesday that the boards of SpaceX and Tesla had separately formed special committees to discuss the idea of a merger, taking a small step toward the possible consolidation of his two biggest companies. Musk, who is the CEO of both companies, said that the special committees had not reached an agreement and that there was no guarantee they would. He said a merger would require support from both sets of shareholders. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said. Musk spoke about the potential tie-up during a call with Wall Street analysts about SpaceX’s quarterly results, which surpassed estimates; the company’s revenue more than doubled in part from renting out computing capacity to other artificial intelligence firms. There has been intense speculation in the stock market over whether a combination might happen, and the two companies already overlap in some areas, including semiconductor manufacturing . In January, Tesla announced that it was investing about $2 billion to acquire shares in an AI startup that’s a subsidiary of SpaceX. Musk said that, because he’s a conflicted party under securities regulations, he is not a member of either special committee or involved in the talks. He said the committees consist of the two boards’ independent directors but did not specify the memberships. items.t: Musk Says ASML and Others Are Expediting Chipmaking Gear for Terafab

items.t: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
items.d: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.
items.fullText: SpaceX’s data centers and Grok agents were more profitable than investors expected in the third quarter of the year, as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on artificial intelligence, which now makes up 52% of its income. CEO Elon Musk’s deep tech conglomerate reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to its regulatory filing . That number was driven by growth in all segments, but especially its renamed “Super Intelligence” business line, which generated $7.5 billion in revenue from the recently acquired Cursor coding tool, Grok bot, and most importantly, the company’s burgeoning neocloud business, which now boasts 1.7 GW of compute. The AI business generated $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition. The top-line revenue number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income that might be attributed to a SpaceX investment in another company. The growing revenue is balanced against total capital expenditures of $19.6 billion, as SpaceX continues to build out a second data center project, Colossus II, and increase investment in Starship, the heavy-lift rocket it sees as vital to deploying a new generation of Starlink satellites and developing orbital data centers. CFO Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter. items.fullText: 핫픽! 미국주식 핫픽! 미국주식 "테슬라·스페이스X합병발표?"…스페이스X 실적발표에 쏠린 눈 입력 2026.10.21 00:01 수정 2026.10.21 00:01 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김정아 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. AI 기사요약 스페이스X가 AI 사업 성장과 스타링크의 실적 호조에 힘입어 3분기 첫 흑자 전환을 기록할 것으로 전망되는 가운데, 시장에서는 일론 머스크가 이끄는 테슬라와의 합병 및 AI 분야 시너지 창출 가능성에 주목하고 있습니다. "합병 발표시 테슬라 주주들, 주당 480달러 수용 전망" 스페이스X 3분기 실적 예상 넘어 흑자전환 전망 AI 부문 매출 26억달러에서 63억달러로 증가 예상 사진=AFP 스페이스X의 3분기 실적이 미국 동부 시간으로 20일 오후 장 마감후에 발표된다.월가는 이번 분기에 스페이스X가 흑자로 전환할 것으로 예상하고 있다. 또 이 회사에서 유일하게 수익을 내고 있는 사업부인 스타링크의 실적 이상으로 인공지능(AI) 부문의 실적에 주시하고 있다. 이와 함께 테슬라의 실적에 하루 앞서 발표되는 이 날, 혹시 테슬라와의 합병을 발표하지 않을까 하는 기대도 적지 않다. 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. items.t: SpaceX alum’s aviation startup, Reliable Robotics, lands $115M, topping $1B valuation
items.d: Reliable Robotics extended its Series D round with $115 million in equity and $25 million in debt.
items.fullText: Reliable Robotics has been working for nearly a decade to commercialize autonomous flying technology that can be installed on existing aircraft. Now, with a $115 million funding boost, the Mountain View, California-based startup has a longer runway as it pushes to get its autonomous flight system certified by the Federal Aviation Administration — a critical milestone that co-founder and CEO Robert Rose said the startup is inching toward. The financing is an extension of its Series D round and includes $90 million in equity funding led by Nimble Partners and $25 million in debt from Silicon Valley Bank. The Series D round, which now totals $275 million, has pushed the startup’s valuation beyond the $1 billion mark. Other investors include Gideon Strategic Partners, RockCreek, Geek Ventures, Gold Hill Capital, Sparkwave Capital, and others. Reliable has raised $380 million to date. “We continue to make steady progress and deliver evidence to the FAA and every day, we inch closer and closer,” said Rose, a former director of flight software at SpaceX who has also had stints at Tesla and Google. Reliable co-founder and CTO Juerg Frefel is also a SpaceX veteran who spent nearly a decade there as an engineer. And in aviation — one of the most regulated industries in the world — moving toward certification of new technology is progress. Reliable Robotics is working to gain FAA certification on four fronts, all of which are linked to its goal of autonomous flight. Its first product, called continuous autopilot engagement, handles the engine startup, taxiing, takeoff, and landing for the pilot, who remains in the aircraft and interacts with the autonomous flight system through a touchscreen. Rose expects to receive certification for this critical first system in 18 to 24 months. items.t: Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie
items.d: Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Elon Musk and Anthropic make promises to give the public a piece of the AI pie The promises come as the public has broadly soured on AI and concerns about its economic impact grow. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Elon Musk is awarded the National Medal of Science during the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 19, 2026, 10:39 AM EDT By Rob Wile Elon Musk and officials at AI giant Anthropic are pledging to give coveted shares in their companies to the general public as concerns about AI’s economic and societal impact continue to pile up . “Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America,” Musk posted on X on Monday. “This will be the first of many.” One SpaceX share is currently valued at about $150. With approximately 72 million children under the age of 18 in the U.S., Musk’s donation would currently be worth about $10.8 billion — less than 2% of his current net worth. He provided no additional information. Musk could not be reached for additional comment. His statement comes one day after officials at Anthropic said the company would commit 5% of company shares to a “public benefit fund” in order to address “labor market impacts” of AI. In a statement, Anthropic officials said the fund could make charitable donations or direct money to “specific populations,” emphasizing the fund’s “versatility.” “Given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed,” they said. Anthropic has been preparing for an initial public offering — releasing its stock for trading on public markets — that analysts say would value the company at more than $1 trillion. The company has long championed employees’ charitable giving by promising to match their donations. Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic. items.t: Elon Musk shows off ‘flying’ Tesla Roadster after years of delays
items.d: Elon Musk showed off the new Tesla Roadster prototype Thursday that can briefly launch itself into the air using rocket-inspired thrusters.
items.fullText: Tech News Elon Musk shows off ‘flying’ Tesla Roadster after years of delays The electric sports car performed aerial stunts using thrusters developed with SpaceX, but it’s still years from production, and its flying features aren’t approved for public roads. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tesla unveils its next generation 'flying' Roadster 03:33 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 16, 2026, 11:58 AM EDT By Chris Perez Elon Musk showed off a new vehicle prototype Thursday that can briefly launch itself into the air using rocket-inspired thrusters. The Tesla Roadster made its debut eight years after it was first announced. The company has yet to announce a price or release date, though the Tesla and SpaceX CEO said production would not begin until 2028. In a stunt-filled demonstration at a SpaceX testing facility in Texas, Musk told the live audience that what they were about to see “was not AI or SI.” The vehicle, a collaboration between Tesla and SpaceX, then slowly drove up a curved ramp shaped like half of a roller coaster loop before accelerating and launching itself off the ramp, hurdling over five other Tesla vehicles and bringing itself to a soft landing in a cloud of condensation using cold-gas thrusters. “Well, it worked!” Musk said after the stunt, adding that “it’s not necessarily a safety-optimized car.” Tesla Tesla says a fan-based suction system creates downforce to hold the vehicle against the road’s surface, while self-refilling cold-gas thrusters power its airborne maneuvers.
